samples.summary: New `text/plain` assertion is truthiness-only over an all-empty-cell fixture, so it cannot tell the right table from the wrong one
samples.evidence: `expect(written.get('text/plain'), 'empty text/plain flavour').toBeTruthy()` only distinguishes '' from non-''. The fixture is built with `createTableBlock(3, 2)` / `createTableBlock(1, 1)` (test lines 119-125), and `createTableBlock` fills cells via `createTableCell()` with empty paragraphs (src/model/types.ts:656-676), so every cell's text is ''. The produced string is just separators ('\t\n\t\n\t'), which is identical to what resolving the *outer* table (or any other 3-row-ish shape) would produce. It catches the exact '' regression the diff fixed, but any wrong-table / wrong-cell-rectangle resolution in `getSelectedText` would pass unnoticed. Giving one or two inner cells real inline text and asserting the exact tab/newline string would make the assertion meaningful.

samples.summary: The two new cycle-guard tests assert values that hold trivially; their only real signal is 'did not hang', and the stated vitest-timeout rescue does not apply to a synchronous infinite loop
samples.evidence: Both new tests pass a layout with `blocks: []` (cyclicLayout(), test lines 288-300), so `getNormalizedRange(...) === null` (selection.ts: `anchorIdx === -1` → null) and `resolvePositionPixel(...) === undefined` (peer-cursor.ts: `layout.blocks.find(...)` → `!lb?.layoutTable` → undefined) are true for many reasons unrelated to the guard — the assertions cannot distinguish a correct guard from an unrelated early return. The discriminating behaviour is termination, and the test comment (lines 285-286) claims "vitest's per-test timeout is what turns that into a failure rather than a wedged suite"; vitest timeouts are event-loop based and cannot interrupt a synchronous `while` loop, so a removed guard in `walkToTopLevelBlockId` would wedge the worker rather than produce a failing test (the peer-cursor one additionally `unshift`es unboundedly and would OOM). Bounding the walk and asserting the returned/stopped id (or using a non-empty `blocks` array so the trivial path is closed) would give these tests a real assertion.

verdict.reason: The cell-internal nested-aware branch of getSelectedText (selection.ts:813-821, fallback to resolveNestedTableLayout) has no test asserting the text/plain flavour. The only test that selects text inside a nested table's cell, copy-integrity.test.ts:354-371, asserts solely payloadBlocks(...), and payloadBlocks (copy-integrity.test.ts:194-198) reads only WAFFLEDOCS_MIME, which handleCopy fills from getSelectedBlocks() — a different call from getSelectedText (text-editor.ts:1443-1446); that test would stay green if the nested fallback were reverted to the flat layout.blocks.find. I searched repo-wide (all *.test.ts, *.spec.ts, *.test.tsx, *.spec.tsx across every package) for 'text/plain' and 'getSelectedText'; every text/plain assertion in docs tests is body text, a flat table cell, a header/footer, or the *cell-range* branch (nested-table-cell-range.test.ts:250 via shiftClickRects). clipboard.ts exports only WAFFLEDOCS_MIME (clipboard.ts:458) — no plain-text constant that could hide an aliased assertion. Impact is major: getSelectedText feeds text/plain on copy (text-editor.ts:1446) and on cut (text-editor.ts:1492), where deleteSelection() runs unconditionally at text-editor.ts:1494, so a regression silently deletes the nested-cell text while writing an empty clipboard, undetected by any test.
